$comment: Networks offered to someone who has none. One file, read by both clients — the desktop imports it, the Android build copies it into assets. Everything here was confirmed by connecting on 2026-09-10; `checked` on each entry says what came back. Sizes move, so treat the counts as the order of magnitude they were, not as a promise.

networks.name: Libera.Chat
networks.description: Free and open-source projects. Started in 2021 by the people who had been running freenode, and where most of those communities moved.
networks.checked: solanum, 30 servers, about 31,600 people, SASL (PLAIN, EXTERNAL, SCRAM-SHA-512, ECDSA)

networks.name: IRCnet
networks.description: One half of the 1990 split that made IRC two networks. Still large, still mostly European, and still without network-wide nick registration.
networks.checked: ircd 2.12, 34 servers, about 15,800 people. The round-robin open.ircnet.net cannot be verified over TLS — each server presents a certificate for its own name — so this points at one that can.

networks.name: Undernet
networks.description: Running since 1992. Channels are looked after by a bot called X rather than by ChanServ.
networks.checked: ircu 2.10.12, 33 servers, about 16,400 people. Port 6697 could not be reached from the machine this was checked on; 6667 answered.

networks.name: OFTC
networks.description: The Open and Free Technology Community — Debian, Tor, and the projects around them.
networks.checked: hybrid 7.2, 17 servers, about 14,200 people. No SASL: log in to NickServ instead.

networks.name: Rizon
networks.description: Anime, manga and general chat. Large, social, and busy at all hours.

networks.name: EFnet
networks.description: The other half of the 1990 split, and the oldest network still running. Nothing is registered here: no NickServ, no ChanServ, no account.
networks.checked: ircd-ratbox 3.0, 20 servers, about 8,400 people. The round-robin irc.efnet.org cannot be verified over TLS, so this points at one server that can.

networks.name: DALnet
networks.description: Running since 1994, and where NickServ and ChanServ were invented.
networks.checked: bahamut 2.2, 35 servers, about 6,500 people. No SASL: log in to NickServ instead.

networks.name: QuakeNet
networks.description: Gaming, and the largest network in Europe for much of the 2000s. Channels are looked after by a bot called Q.
networks.checked: snircd 1.3, 25 servers, about 5,400 people. Port 6697 could not be reached from the machine this was checked on; 6667 answered.

networks.name: hackint
networks.description: The hacker community around the Chaos Computer Club and the European hackerspaces.

networks.name: EsperNet
networks.description: Game development and Minecraft modding projects.

networks.name: Snoonet
networks.description: Communities that grew out of Reddit, and a general-purpose network besides.
networks.checked: InspIRCd 3, 11 servers, about 1,200 people, SASL (PLAIN, EXTERNAL)

networks.name: tilde.chat
networks.description: The tilde community: shared public-access Unix servers, and the people who run them.
